title: House Ethics Report Accused Gaetz of Sex With a 17-Year-Old at a 2017 Party
description_short: A December 2024 House Ethics report described an allegation involving Gaetz and a 17-year-old at a 2017 party; AP said there was no evidence he knew her age.
description_medium: On December 23, 2024, the House Ethics Committee released a report with dissenting views about former Representative Matt Gaetz. AP reported that the report accused him of paying for sex, including in an incident involving a 17-year-old at a 2017 party. AP also reported the committee said there was no evidence he knew her age. This corrected event is the report’s release, not a public hearing in summer 2024.
description_long: On December 23, 2024, the House Ethics Committee released its report on former Representative Matt Gaetz, including dissenting views. The report addressed allegations involving sexual misconduct and drug use. The Associated Press reported that the committee accused Gaetz of paying for sex, including in an incident involving a 17-year-old girl at a 2017 party, and said the committee cited her testimony and corroborating witnesses. AP also reported that the woman told the committee she had not told Gaetz she was under 18 and that he learned her age more than a month after the party. The committee report is the basis for describing the allegation; it is not a public hearing transcript from summer 2024, as the original title implied. AP reported that the report helped sink Gaetz’s nomination for attorney general. This card records the report and its attributed findings, not a criminal conviction or a direct Trump policy action. The account remains attributed to the committee and the reporting, and the committee’s statement about Gaetz’s knowledge is included to avoid implying that he knew the girl’s age at the time.

title: Trump Said He Instructed DOJ to Terminate Remaining Biden-Era U.S. Attorneys
description_short: Reuters reported that Trump instructed DOJ to terminate remaining Biden-era U.S. attorneys; the evidence does not show an overnight firing and replacement of all 93.
description_medium: On February 18, 2025, Trump said he had instructed the Justice Department to terminate all remaining Biden-era U.S. attorneys, Reuters reported. He said the department had been “politicized like never before” and posted that the administration must “clean house” immediately. Reuters also described earlier termination notices and departures. This supports a reported instruction, not the original claim of a first-night purge or loyalist replacements by dawn.
description_long: Reuters reported that on February 18, 2025, President Donald Trump said he had instructed the Justice Department to terminate all remaining Biden-era U.S. attorneys. Trump said the department had been “politicized like never before” and wrote that the administration must “clean house” immediately and restore confidence. Reuters said the White House had sent termination notices the previous week to several U.S. attorneys appointed by Joe Biden, while several others announced departures and others had left government. The corrected event is Trump’s reported instruction and its stated target, not a completed firing of every U.S. attorney. The supplied record does not support its original claim that all 93 sitting attorneys were fired on January 20 and replaced by dawn. Reuters did not report a nationwide roster of loyalist replacements in this account. The article distinguishes the February statement from the earlier transition: some attorneys received notices, while others announced or had already made departures. This entry preserves what Reuters reported Trump said and does not claim that DOJ completed every termination, that the action bypassed Senate confirmation, or that a court found the instruction unlawful.

title: April 2025 Trump Administration Plan Proposed Cutting the CDC Budget by More Than 40%
description_short: CNN reported an April 10 internal plan proposed a CDC budget reduction of more than 40%; the draft could change and was not an enacted cut.
description_medium: An internal federal health-agency document dated April 10, 2025, proposed reducing the CDC budget by more than 40%, CNN reported on April 16. CNN said the draft could still be finalized with changes and would consolidate health programs into a proposed Administration for a Healthy America. This corrected card concerns a proposal, not a March cut already in effect or proof that every surveillance program named in the original synopsis ended.
description_long: CNN reported on April 16, 2025, that an internal Trump administration document dated April 10 outlined a proposed reduction of more than 40% in the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s budget. The document also previewed a broader restructuring of federal health agencies and consolidation of programs into a proposed Administration for a Healthy America. CNN reported that the plan could still be finalized with changes and described the reductions as what would happen “if enacted as is.” The evidence supports a proposed budget action; it does not show that the CDC had already received a 40% reduction in March. Nor does the accessed reporting substantiate that every program named in the original synopsis—including outbreak-detection grants, chronic-disease programs, global surveillance across 49 countries, and state emergency-preparedness agreements—was eliminated by this same proposal. This card therefore focuses on the April 10 proposal and leaves implementation unresolved. It does not combine the proposal, agency layoffs, and program closures into one completed event. The percentage is CNN’s description of the administration’s plan, not a final appropriation or an independently audited spending change.
